github._notes: GitHub App: endpoints hardcoded from GitHub's documentation (GitHub also serves undocumented RFC 8414 metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/login/oauth, observed 2026-09-30); scopes come from App permissions, so the ceiling is empty; revocation uses GitHub's grant-deletion API, the documented RFC 7009 deviation.

linear._notes: Linear's MCP authorization server. The broker is a client registered once with tools/register-mcp-client.py (DCR); the client secret expires after 90 days. Tokens are bound to the read-only MCP server (Linear's full MCP server refuses them). Linear refuses `resource` on refresh but keeps the refreshed token bound, hence resource_on_refresh false. 24h access tokens, rotating refresh tokens (reuse fails). Revoking the refresh token does not revoke the access token, so the broker revokes both. No REST user endpoint: vendor_user_id is 'unknown'.

atlassian._notes: Atlassian's MCP authorization server (Rovo MCP). The broker is a client registered once with tools/register-mcp-client.py (DCR); an org admin must allow the broker's callback origin under Rovo MCP server domain settings. Read and search scopes only (enforced by Atlassian). 8h access tokens, rotating refresh tokens. No REST user endpoint for these tokens: vendor_user_id is 'unknown'.

cloudflare._notes: Cloudflare's MCP authorization server (mcp.cloudflare.com, code-mode tools search/docs/execute). Registered once with tools/register-mcp-client.py (DCR). Cloudflare grants exactly the requested scopes, so this read-only ceiling makes even `execute` read-only. 1h access tokens, rotating refresh tokens. The registration's client secret expires (about 90 days) and cannot be rotated: re-register and have users reconnect. vendor_user_id is 'unknown'.

mockhub._notes: Test vendor AS (tests/stack/mock-vendor): RFC 8414 discovery, 60s access tokens, rotating refresh tokens with replay-revokes-family, RFC 7009 revocation. Exists so the single-flight and revocation gates run headless.

mockhub-jwt._notes: Same test AS via private_key_jwt (RFC 7523): the broker signs a client assertion with the private key held in vendor-clients/mockhub-jwt ({client_id, private_key, alg}); the mock verifies it for real. Exists so the pkj leg of the client-auth matrix runs headless.

mockhub-norevoke._notes: Same test AS, but its metadata advertises no revocation_endpoint. Exists so the delete-without-vendor-revocation path runs headless (local delete, audited outcome: unsupported).

mockhub-atlassian._notes: Test AS playing Atlassian's own MCP sign-in: tokens are bound to the resource, and the mock-mcp stand-in at /atlassian/mcp refuses tokens issued for anything else. Exists so the RFC 8707 resource path runs headless.

mockhub-cloudflare._notes: Test AS playing Cloudflare's own MCP sign-in: tokens are bound to the resource, and the mock-mcp stand-in at /cloudflare/mcp refuses tokens issued for anything else. Exists so the RFC 8707 resource path runs headless.
